findings.text: The done_when requires the importer population of reckon.crew.findings, reckon.crew.review_records and reckon.crew.plan_review to add no failure against the base revision, and no result is recorded: the head gate ran four named test files and logs/importer-suite-head.log is zero bytes, while 80 test files import plan_review, which is the module this hook line changes.

The persisted-index scaffolding added here duplicates what review_records.py already owns at review_records.py:1014 (_index_sources), :1024 (the _INDEX_CODE_STAMP memo, whose comment is copied verbatim) and :1040 (_index_cache_path); the addition neither extends nor generalises that owner, so a fix to one index's staleness rule does not reach the other.

The code-review root is read by naming plan_review's private _code_review_store_dir and CODE_REVIEW_FILE_PREFIX, replacing the public list_code_reviews call whose docstring gave the reason for preferring it; behaviour is equivalent today, but findings.py now carries its own copy of that store layout.

justifications.durability: tests/test_findings_are_read_from_a_write_time_index.py:389 withholds note_record_written and asserts the same read opens exactly one record, so reinstating the regression reddens the control.
justifications.evidence: logs/gate-head.log records 41 passed with a red control and three sub-2 s timings under load, while the importer-population arm has a zero-byte log at logs/importer-suite-head.log.
justifications.fit: findings.py:787 reaches into plan_review._code_review_store_dir and CODE_REVIEW_FILE_PREFIX, replacing the public list_code_reviews that owned the store layout.
justifications.goal_fidelity: findings.py:964 answers from a persisted document covering both roots, and review_records.py:296, plan_review.py:2348 and plan_review.py:5429 are the three writer hooks the plan named.
justifications.reuse: findings.py:480 and findings.py:498 re-implement review_records.py:1024 and review_records.py:1040 without extending review_records.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff --stat 50f121aa..fba33c99 names only the five declared write paths, and the added response row field is what done_when case two reads back.

verdicts.diff: Read commit by commit against the base: 45476b9efe adds the persisted index and the thirteen-case test, 64d92d8a5a adds the parent-listing cache, 5bf2be09ac adds the evidence fragment and its timings, and every hunk stays inside the five declared paths.
verdicts.done_when: The done_when asks for six cases plus writer controls in tests/test_findings_are_read_from_a_write_time_index.py, a red index-deleted control, three sub-2 s fresh-process reads with load logged, the importer population adding no failure, and ruff clean; the gate records 41 passed at head against 28 at base with the control red and timings 1.069/1.281/1.871 s at load 88.4/86.4/81.5, while the importer arm has a zero-byte log.
verdicts.goal: The goal is to persist the findings index in the node-local cache, have the three record writers update it, and read it in findings_by_path; findings.py:964 now answers from _indexed_rows, which loads and persists that document, and both roots are indexed (committed tree at findings.py:740, code-review store at findings.py:798).
verdicts.manifest: Read; it records status complete, four commits, the six cases plus three writer cases and their withheld-hook controls, the red negative control, the 41-vs-28 gate pair and the delivered-head timings, and is silent on the importer-population arm and on the ruff clause of its own done_when.
verdicts.write_paths: The manifest declares findings.py, review_records.py, plan_review.py, the new test and the evidence fragment; git diff --stat 50f121aa..fba33c99 names exactly those five paths and nothing else.
